events.title: iPhone 5S released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone 5S on September 20, 2013 — debuting Touch ID fingerprint authentication and the 64-bit A7 chip.
events.about: Touch ID enabled secure app login and Apple Pay foundations; the A7 made 64-bit ARM mainstream and pushed [Android] OEMs to match. Developers gained LocalAuthentication APIs and a performance ceiling for AR and graphics-heavy apps years earlier than expected.

narrative.whyChosen: The 5S made biometrics and 64-bit mobile CPUs standard expectations.
narrative.whyImportant: Fingerprint auth and 64-bit chips changed security and performance baselines for mobile dev.
narrative.problemSolved: Phone unlock and payment auth relied on PINs; mobile CPUs were still treated as 32-bit platforms.

events.title: iPhone 5C released
events.summary: Apple shipped the colorful iPhone 5C alongside the 5S on September 20, 2013 — a plastic-bodied model targeting mid-tier buyers.
events.about: The 5C expanded [iOS] reach with a lower price point while running the same [iOS] 7 stack developers already targeted. It showed Apple would segment hardware without fragmenting the software platform.

narrative.whyChosen: The 5C tested whether Apple could sell a colorful mid-range iPhone without splitting the developer stack.
narrative.whyImportant: One [iOS] target across premium and mid-tier hardware simplified mobile development.
narrative.problemSolved: Premium-only iPhones limited [iOS] audience growth in price-sensitive markets.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note 3 released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note 3 — 1080p display and [USB] 3.0 — productivity-focused phablet peak.
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on Android. 1080p display and usb 3.0 — productivity-focused phablet peak. Note apps and split-screen Android development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note 3 advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen Android productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: Android lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.
